Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a scope exclusion; 'should not apply'
Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: this Regulation should not apply to public authorities of a third country and international organisations when acting in the framework of cooperation or international agreements concluded at Union or national level for law enforcement and judicial cooperation
Note: Scope exemption, conditional: 'provided that the relevant third country or international organisation provides adequate safeguards'. Same recital extends scope to third-country providers/deployers whose output is used in the Union.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a scope exclusion
Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: It is therefore necessary to exclude from its scope AI systems and models specifically developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development.
Note: Also: product-oriented research, testing and development before placing on the market is out of scope, without prejudice to sandboxes and real-world testing; research 'should be carried out in accordance with recognised ethical and professional standards'.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a prohibition; 'should therefore be prohibited'
Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of certain AI systems with the objective to or the effect of materially distorting human behaviour
Note: Prohibition of manipulative/deceptive techniques causing significant harm, and of exploiting vulnerabilities (age, disability, social or economic situation). Binds any provider or deployer, including public authorities. Intention to cause harm not needed.

If not met: use 'should be authorised only if' registered, unless provided otherwise
Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement authority
Quote: unless provided otherwise in this Regulation, has registered the system in the database as set out in this Regulation
Note: Registration in the EU database (see recital (131): law enforcement registrations go in a secure non-public section). Also coded Delivery (FRIA).

Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement authority
Quote: as determined in national law and specified in the context of each individual urgent use case by the law enforcement authority itself
Note: In urgency, use 'should be restricted to the absolute minimum necessary and should be subject to appropriate safeguards and conditions'; the authority itself specifies them per use. Also coded Accountability (retrospective request).

Position: public authority: member state
Quote: should only be possible where and in as far as the Member State concerned has decided to expressly provide for the possibility to authorise such use in its detailed rules of national law
Note: 'Member States remain free under this Regulation not to provide for such a possibility at all' or to allow it only for some objectives.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a prohibition; 'should be prohibited'
Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: to predict the occurrence of an actual or potential criminal offence based solely on profiling them or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics should be prohibited
Note: Individual crime-risk assessment based solely on profiling. Principle: no judgement on AI-predicted behaviour 'without human assessment thereof'. Carve-out: risk analytics not based on profiling individuals, e.g. tools 'by customs authorities' to locate narcotics or illicit goods.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a derogation from high-risk classification
Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation); applied by the provider
Position: public authority: EU institution; outside the state: private companies (providers)
Quote: The first such condition should be that the AI system is intended to perform a narrow procedural task, such as an AI system that transforms unstructured data into structured data, an AI system that classifies incoming documents into categories
Note: Annex-listed systems that do not materially influence decision-making may be non-high-risk. Four conditions: narrow procedural task; improving a previously completed human activity; detecting decision patterns or deviations (not replacing human assessment 'without proper human review'); preparatory task (e.g. file handling, translation). The provider makes the determination (see Delivery and Accountability entries for this recital). Directly relevant to public-sector document classification tools.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); limit on the derogation
Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: AI systems used in high-risk use-cases listed in an annex to this Regulation should be considered to pose significant risks of harm to the health, safety or fundamental rights if the AI system implies profiling
Note: Profiling (GDPR/LED/EUDPR definitions) always keeps an annex-listed system high-risk.

Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: AI systems used in employment, workers management and access to self-employment, in particular for the recruitment and selection of persons, for making decisions affecting terms of the work-related relationship
Note: These 'should also be classified as high-risk'; includes task allocation and monitoring/evaluation of workers. Applies to public bodies as employers [inference].

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a classification exemption
Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: AI systems specifically intended to be used for administrative proceedings by tax and customs authorities as well as by financial intelligence units
Note: These 'should not be classified as high-risk AI systems used by law enforcement authorities' for criminal-offence purposes. Public-sector scope exemption.

Position: public authority: law enforcement and other relevant authorities [inference]
Quote: The impact of the use of AI tools on the defence rights of suspects should not be ignored
Note: Names 'the difficulty in challenging their results in court'; gives no mechanism, holder or consequence. Same recital: 'The use of AI tools by law enforcement and other relevant authorities should not become a factor of inequality, or exclusion.' Coded for the challenge question; thin.

Position: outside the state: private companies (providers can also be public bodies)
Quote: The measures adopted by the providers to comply with the mandatory requirements of this Regulation should take into account the generally acknowledged state of the art on AI, be proportionate and effective
Note: Comparator for all provider checks: 'generally acknowledged state of the art'. Providers of products under NLF legislation may fold testing and documentation into existing procedures.

Position: outside the state: private companies (providers can also be public bodies)
Quote: This process should ensure that the provider identifies risks or adverse impacts and implements mitigation measures for the known and reasonably foreseeable risks of AI systems to the health, safety and fundamental rights
Note: Risk-management system: 'continuous, iterative process ... throughout the entire lifecycle', 'regularly reviewed and updated'. Covers intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable misuse. Trigger: ongoing. Comparator: state of the art. Metric: not stated.

Holder: Relevant competent authorities, including sectoral ones
Position: public authority: competent authorities
Quote: Relevant competent authorities, including sectoral ones, providing or supporting the access to data may also support the provision of high-quality data for the training, validation and testing of AI systems.
Note: Data access as a resource; permissive ('may').

Position: outside the state: private companies (providers can also be public bodies)
Quote: Measures taken by providers to ensure compliance with those principles may include not only anonymisation and encryption, but also the use of technology that permits algorithms to be brought to the data
Note: Principles are data minimisation and data protection by design and by default from Union data protection law, which 'are applicable'; privacy 'must be guaranteed throughout the entire lifecycle'.

Position: outside the state: private companies (providers); mixed incl. public authorities (deployers)
Quote: Deployers should, inter alia, be in a better position to make the correct choice of the system that they intend to use in light of the obligations applicable to them
Note: Transparency and instructions for use as a resource for the deployer's decision on whether and which system to use, and on intended and precluded uses.

Position: public authority: member state
Quote: Instructions for use should be made available in a language which can be easily understood by target deployers, as determined by the Member State concerned.
Note: Member State sets the language; providers make instructions available.

Holder: the provider of the system (measures); the human operator (control)
Position: outside the state: private companies (provider); mixed (operator in deployer organisation)
Quote: the system is subject to in-built operational constraints that cannot be overridden by the system itself and is responsive to the human operator
Note: Human control over the system built into design; authority sits with the human operator.

Position: outside the state: private companies
Quote: serving as their contact person established in the Union
Note: Contact point for third-country providers. Also coded Accountability.

Holder: operators along the value chain (e.g. importers and distributors)
Position: mixed: operators (mainly private companies)
Quote: those operators could act in more than one role at the same time and should therefore fulfil cumulatively all relevant obligations associated with those roles
Note: Allocation of responsibility by role; would cover a public body acting as both provider and deployer [inference].

Position: outside the state: private companies
Quote: the former provider should nonetheless closely cooperate and make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance
Note: Condition: 'when that provider has not expressly excluded the change of the AI system into a high-risk AI system'. Serves conformity assessment by the new provider (e.g. a public body that becomes provider [inference]).

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); 'should be performed', 'should be updated'
Position: public authority: bodies governed by public law; outside the state: private entities providing public services
Quote: The impact assessment should be performed prior to deploying the high-risk AI system, and should be updated when the deployer considers that any of the relevant factors have changed.
Note: Triggers: before deployment; on change (deployer's judgement). Content: deployer's processes, period and frequency of use, categories of persons affected, specific risks of harm to fundamental rights. Compares against fundamental rights; metric not stated.
Quote check: ok in pieces (crosses a page break, footnote or extraction gap)

Level of obligation: n/a (provided by provider; deployer 'should take into account')
Holder: the provider of the high-risk AI system (supplies information); the deployer (uses it)
Position: outside the state: private companies (provider); public authority or private entity (deployer)
Quote: the deployer should take into account information relevant to a proper assessment of the impact, including but not limited to the information given by the provider of the high-risk AI system in the instructions for use
Note: Information from the instructions for use serving the FRIA.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); example of measures ('could be instrumental')
Position: public authority: bodies governed by public law; outside the state: private entities providing public services
Quote: complaint handling and redress procedures, as they could be instrumental in mitigating risks to fundamental rights in concrete use-cases
Note: Complaint and redress named as an example of measures the deployer should determine; not a free-standing duty in the recital.

Holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: should be subject to exceptions as regards the transparency-related requirements imposed on general-purpose AI models, unless they can be considered to present a systemic risk
Note: Applies to providers of GPAI models released under free and open-source licence with public weights, architecture and usage information. Exception does not cover the training-content summary or the copyright policy.

Holder: not stated (codes facilitated by the AI Office; providers as users)
Position: public authority: EU institution (AI Office) [inference]
Quote: Providers should be able to rely on codes of practice to demonstrate compliance with the obligations.
Note: Means of demonstrating compliance for GPAI providers. Also: harmonised standards, once assessed as suitable by the AI Office, give a presumption of conformity; otherwise 'alternative adequate means'.

Position: outside the state: European standardisation organisations [inference]
Quote: Standardisation should play a key role to provide technical solutions to providers to ensure compliance with this Regulation, in line with the state of the art
Note: Harmonised standards 'should be a means for providers to demonstrate conformity'. Developer of standards not named in this sentence (European standardisation organisations on Commission request [inference]). Balanced stakeholder representation in standard-setting 'should ... be encouraged'.

Position: public authority: member state
Quote: Member States should not create unjustified obstacles to the placing on the market or the putting into service of high-risk AI systems that comply with the requirements laid down in this Regulation and bear the CE marking
Note: Limits Member State authority over compliant systems.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: The Commission should develop guidelines to specify the elements of the quality management system to be fulfilled in this simplified manner by microenterprises.
Note: Microenterprises may fulfil QMS duty in a simplified manner; guidance serves the QMS requirement (recital (81)).

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: the Commission facilitates, to the extent possible, access to testing and experimentation facilities to bodies, groups or laboratories established or accredited pursuant to any relevant Union harmonisation legislation
Note: Serves conformity-assessment bodies (e.g. medical device expert panels and laboratories).

Position: public authority: EU bodies [inference]
Quote: a Board composed of representatives of the Member States, a scientific panel to integrate the scientific community and an advisory forum to contribute stakeholder input to the implementation of this Regulation, at Union and national level, should be established
Note: Governance framework 'to coordinate and support the application of this Regulation at national level'. The AI Office's mission (set by Commission Decision) not coded: report of another instrument / a body's own mandate.

Position: public authority: member state
Quote: such representatives may be any persons belonging to public entities who should have the relevant competences and powers to facilitate coordination at national level
Note: Competence and powers of Board members, serving Board coordination.

Statutory: statutory: AI Act recital (179) (recital, not an operative article)
Position: public authority: member state
Quote: Member States should lay down and notify to the Commission the rules on penalties, including administrative fines
Note: Sanctions to be in place and 'properly and effectively implemented by the date of application'. Notification to the Commission is also a Coordination link. Operative provision Art. 99(1)-(2) (outside this part).

Holder: not stated (the Regulation sets its scope)
Position: not stated (EU legislature)
Quote: This Regulation applies neither to public authorities in a third country nor to international organisations
Note: Condition: where they use AI systems 'in the framework of international cooperation or agreements for law enforcement and judicial cooperation with the Union or with one or more Member States, provided that such a third country or international organisation provides adequate safeguards with respect to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals'. Who judges adequacy is not stated.

If not met: not stated here; EDPS may fine Union bodies (Art. 100, outside this part; see recital 168)
Holder: Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies (answerable); the European Data Protection Supervisor (forum)
Position: public authority: EU institutions and bodies; EU independent supervisory body
Quote: as regards AI systems put into service or used by Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies, references to national competent authorities or market surveillance authorities in this Regulation shall be construed as references to the European Data Protection Supervisor
Note: EU institutions using or putting AI into service answer to the EDPS in its capacity as market surveillance/competent authority. Also coded Decision-making/Design (same passage).

If not met: not stated in Art. 5; Art. 99(3) (outside this part): administrative fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or up to 7% of worldwide annual turnover; Union bodies up to EUR 1 500 000 (Art. 100(2)); each Member State sets the extent to which fines may be imposed on its public authorities (Art. 99(8))
Holder: not stated (applies to anyone placing on the market, putting into service or using)
Position: not stated (EU legislature); bound actors include public authorities as providers or deployers
Quote: the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person’s consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques
Note: Ban (stop decision set in law). Condition: 'with the objective, or the effect of materially distorting the behaviour' and causing or being reasonably likely to cause 'significant harm'. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

If not met: not stated in Art. 5; Art. 99(3) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7% of turnover; Union bodies up to EUR 1 500 000 (Art. 100(2)); Member States set extent for public authorities (Art. 99(8))
Holder: not stated (applies to anyone placing on the market, putting into service or using)
Position: not stated (EU legislature); bound actors include public authorities
Quote: the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation
Note: Ban where the objective or effect is materially distorting behaviour causing or reasonably likely to cause significant harm. [inference] Relevant to public services dealing with people in vulnerable social or economic situations.

If not met: not stated in Art. 5; Art. 99(3) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7% of turnover; Union bodies up to EUR 1 500 000 (Art. 100(2)); Member States set extent for public authorities (Art. 99(8))
Holder: not stated (applies to anyone placing on the market, putting into service for this purpose or using)
Position: not stated (EU legislature); bound actors include public authorities
Quote: the use of AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage
Note: Ban on untargeted scraping to build facial recognition databases.

If not met: not stated in Art. 5; Art. 99(3) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7% of turnover; Union bodies up to EUR 1 500 000 (Art. 100(2)); Member States set extent for public authorities (Art. 99(8))
Holder: not stated (applies to anyone placing on the market, putting into service for this purpose or using)
Position: not stated (EU legislature); bound actors include public employers and public education institutions
Quote: the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions
Note: Exception: 'except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons'. Covers public-sector workplaces and public schools/universities.

If not met: not stated in Art. 5; Art. 99(3) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7% of turnover; Union bodies up to EUR 1 500 000 (Art. 100(2)); Member States set extent for public authorities (Art. 99(8))
Holder: not stated (applies to anyone placing on the market, putting into service for this purpose or using)
Position: not stated (EU legislature); bound actors include public authorities
Quote: the use of biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation
Note: Carve-out: does not cover 'any labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets, such as images, based on biometric data or categorizing of biometric data in the area of law enforcement'.

Holder: A provider who considers that an AI system referred to in Annex III is not high-risk
Position: outside the state: private companies (a provider may also be a public authority, Art. 3(3))
Quote: A provider who considers that an AI system referred to in Annex III is not high-risk shall document its assessment before that system is placed on the market or put into service.
Note: The provider itself decides whether the Art. 6(3) exemption applies; no prior approval by an authority is stated. Same passage also coded Delivery/Design (documenting the assessment); registration and disclosure coded Accountability/Design.

Level of obligation: statutory duty (with option to integrate procedures)
If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) for provider obligations
Position: outside the state: private companies (product manufacturers)
Quote: providers shall be responsible for ensuring that their product is fully compliant with all applicable requirements under applicable Union harmonisation legislation
Note: Applies where a product contains an AI system subject to Annex I Section A legislation. Providers may integrate testing, reporting, information and documentation into existing procedures under that legislation, to 'avoid duplication and minimise additional burdens'.

If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(a)
Position: not stated; nearest: providers (private companies or public authorities)
Quote: the human oversight measures referred to in Article 14, including the technical measures put in place to facilitate the interpretation of the outputs of the high-risk AI systems by the deployers
Note: Tools and information for deployers' human oversight (serves Art. 14 and Art. 26(2)).

Level of obligation: statutory duty on provider to enable ('as appropriate and proportionate')
If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(a)
Holder: not stated (passive); nearest: providers (supply the means); natural persons assigned human oversight (use it)
Position: not stated; nearest: providers (private companies or public authorities)
Quote: to intervene in the operation of the high-risk AI system or interrupt the system through a ‘stop’ button or a similar procedure that allows the system to come to a halt in a safe state
Note: Tool for the stop decision (serves Decision-making: stopping a tool in use).

If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(a)
Position: public authority or private body (deployer includes public authorities, Art. 3(4))
Quote: no action or decision is taken by the deployer on the basis of the identification resulting from the system unless that identification has been separately verified
Note: Constrains decisions on biometric identification outputs. Exempted for law enforcement, migration, border control or asylum where Union or national law considers the requirement disproportionate. Also coded Delivery/Design.

If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(a)
Position: not stated; nearest: providers (private companies or public authorities)
Quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
Note: Information given to deployers to check performance against; see also Art. 13(3)(b)(ii).

If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% of turnover; Union bodies Art. 100(3); public authorities per Art. 99(8)
Position: outside the state: private companies (a provider may also be a public authority, Art. 3(3))
Quote: ensure that the high-risk AI system undergoes the relevant conformity assessment procedure as referred to in Article 43, prior to its being placed on the market or put into service
Note: Check before market entry or putting into service. Which procedure (self-assessment by internal control or notified body) is set in Art. 43 (p. 78, coded separately). Followed by declaration of conformity (16(g), Art. 47), CE marking (16(h), Art. 48) and registration (16(i), Art. 49).

If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(j)
Position: outside the state: private companies (a provider may also be a public authority, Art. 3(3))
Quote: it shall immediately investigate the causes, in collaboration with the reporting deployer, where applicable, and inform the market surveillance authorities competent for the high-risk AI system concerned
Note: Reports to the competent MSA and, where applicable, the notified body that issued the certificate, 'in particular, of the nature of the non-compliance and of any relevant corrective action taken'. Consequence not stated here. Also coded Delivery/Design.

If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part)
Position: outside the state: private companies (EU-established representative)
Quote: The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations pursuant to this Regulation.
Note: Must then 'immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority, as well as, where applicable, the relevant notified body, about the termination of the mandate and the reasons therefor'. A check on the provider with reporting to the regulator.

If not met: not stated in Art. 26; Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part)
Holder: not stated (passive); nearest: the deployer of a post-remote biometric identification system
Position: not stated; nearest: public authority: law enforcement deployer
Quote: each use of such high-risk AI systems shall be documented in the relevant police file and shall be made available to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority upon request
Note: Recording each use, 'Regardless of the purpose or deployer'. Also coded Accountability/Design (available to MSA and DPA). Excludes disclosure of sensitive operational data related to law enforcement.

Holder: the Commission (develops and manages the tool)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States, using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission, of each conformity assessment body referred to in paragraph 1.
Note: Tool provided by the Commission serving the notification link (Coordination/Design, Art. 30(2)); also used for changes to notifications (Art. 36(1)).

Holder: not stated (the Regulation sets the presumption); applies to conformity assessment bodies
Position: not stated (EU legislature)
Quote: it shall be presumed to comply with the requirements set out in Article 31 in so far as the applicable harmonised standards cover those requirements
Note: Standards-based route to meeting notified-body requirements: where a body 'demonstrates its conformity with the criteria laid down in the relevant harmonised standards' published in the Official Journal.

If not met: restriction, suspension or withdrawal of the designation (as quoted)
Holder: the notifying authority (holds the notified body to account)
Position: public authority: member-state notifying authority
Quote: If the notifying authority comes to the conclusion that the notified body no longer meets the requirements laid down in Article 31 or that it is failing to fulfil its obligations, it shall restrict, suspend or withdraw the designation
Note: Notified bodies answer to the notifying authority. Trigger: 'sufficient reason to consider' non-compliance; authority 'shall without delay investigate the matter with the utmost diligence', inform the body of objections and 'give it the possibility to make its views known'; sanction depends on seriousness; Commission and other Member States informed immediately. Also bears on Decision-making (stopping a checker).

Holder: the national competent authority of the Member State in which the provider of the system covered by the certificate has its place of business; the notifying authority
Position: public authority: member-state competent authority
Quote: the national competent authority of the Member State in which the provider of the system covered by the certificate has its place of business may extend the provisional validity of the certificates for additional periods of three months
Note: Continuity of approvals after a designation changes. Suspension/restriction (36(8)): certificates stay valid if the notifying authority confirms within one month no risk to health, safety or fundamental rights and sets a remedy timeline, or confirms no certificates will be issued; otherwise the provider must confirm within three months that another notified body is temporarily responsible. Withdrawal (36(9)): valid nine months if the competent authority confirms no risk and another notified body assumes responsibility and completes assessment within 12 months; extensions 'shall not exceed 12 months in total'. Commission, Member States and other notified bodies informed.

Holder: providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models
Position: outside the state: private companies (a provider may also be a public authority, Art. 3(3))
Quote: Where providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models do not comply with the common specifications referred to in paragraph 1, they shall duly justify that they have adopted technical solutions that meet the requirements
Note: Comply-or-justify: equivalent level of protection required. To whom the justification is given is not stated.

Holder: not stated (the Regulation sets the presumption)
Position: not stated (EU legislature)
Quote: High-risk AI systems that have been trained and tested on data reflecting the specific geographical, behavioural, contextual or functional setting within which they are intended to be used shall be presumed to comply
Note: 42(2): systems certified or with a statement of conformity under an EU cybersecurity scheme (Regulation (EU) 2019/881) are presumed to meet Art. 15 cybersecurity requirements to the extent covered.

Level of obligation: statutory duty (choice of procedure where standards applied; notified body mandatory otherwise)
If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(f)
Holder: the provider (of high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III)
Position: outside the state: private companies (a provider may also be a public authority, Art. 3(3))
Quote: the provider shall opt for one of the following conformity assessment procedures
Note: For Annex III point 1 (biometrics): where harmonised standards or common specifications applied, provider chooses (a) internal control (Annex VI) or (b) QMS and technical documentation assessment 'with the involvement of a notified body' (Annex VII). Annex VII is mandatory where standards do not exist, were not applied or only partly applied, or were published with a restriction. Trigger: before placing on the market (Art. 16(f)). Also coded Delivery/Design for the public-authority case.

If not met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(f)
Holder: not stated (passive); nearest: providers; a deployer making a substantial modification becomes provider (Art. 25(1)(b))
Position: not stated; nearest: providers (private companies or public authorities)
Quote: High-risk AI systems that have already been subject to a conformity assessment procedure shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification
Note: Re-check trigger: substantial modification (Art. 3(23)), 'regardless of whether the modified system is intended to be further distributed or continues to be used by the current deployer'. For continuously learning systems, changes 'pre-determined by the provider at the moment of the initial conformity assessment' and documented in Annex IV point 2(f) are not substantial modifications.

Position: outside the state: conformity assessment body established under national law (may be private or public)
Quote: any refusal, restriction, suspension or withdrawal of a Union technical documentation assessment certificate or a quality management system approval issued in accordance with the requirements of Annex VII
Note: Reporting to the notifying authority: certificates and approvals issued (a); refusals, restrictions, suspensions, withdrawals (b); circumstances affecting notification (c); information requests from MSAs (d); on request, activities performed incl. cross-border and subcontracting (e).

Holder: the Commission (decides); market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned (withdraws)
Position: public authority: EU institution; member-state market surveillance authority
Quote: Where the Commission considers the authorisation unjustified, it shall be withdrawn by the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned.
Note: EU-level override of national derogations. 46(5): where a Member State objects within 15 days or the Commission considers the authorisation contrary to Union law or the compliance conclusion unfounded, the Commission consults the Member State; 'The operators concerned shall be consulted and have the possibility to present their views'; Commission decides. 46(7): Annex I Section A products use only their own legislation's derogations.

Level of obligation: statutory right of request; Commission duty to take into account
Holder: a provider whose model has been designated (requests); the Commission (reassesses)
Position: outside the state: private companies; public authority: EU institution
Quote: Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk pursuant to paragraph 4, the Commission shall take the request into account and may decide to reassess
Note: Challenge route against designation. Request must contain 'objective, detailed and new reasons'; earliest six months after designation, and six months after any decision to maintain it.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to detail measurement and calculation methodologies with a view to allowing for comparable and verifiable documentation
Note: Sets measurement standards for Annex XI documentation (in particular points 2(d)-(e)). 53(6): may amend Annexes XI and XII 'in light of evolving technological developments'.

Holder: the authorised representative (of a GPAI model provider)
Position: outside the state: private companies (EU-established representative)
Quote: The mandate shall empower the authorised representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the AI Office or the competent authorities, on all issues related to ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
Note: Answerable party in the EU. Tasks (54(3)): verify Annex XI documentation and Art. 53/55 obligations fulfilled (a Delivery check); keep documentation 10 years; provide AI Office information on reasoned request; cooperate 'including when the model is integrated into AI systems placed on the market or put into service in the Union'. 54(5): terminate mandate if provider acts contrary to obligations and 'immediately inform the AI Office'.

Holder: the Commission (AI Office takes preparatory steps)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: the Commission may provide, by means of implementing acts, common rules for the implementation of the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55
Note: Trigger: 'If, by 2 August 2025, a code of practice cannot be finalised, or if the AI Office deems it is not adequate'. 'Codes of practice shall be ready at the latest by 2 May 2025.'

Holder: market surveillance authorities and notified bodies
Position: public authority: member-state market surveillance authorities; outside the state: conformity assessment bodies
Quote: the exit reports and the written proof provided by the national competent authority shall be taken positively into account by market surveillance authorities and notified bodies
Note: Links sandbox outcomes to later checks, 'with a view to accelerating conformity assessment procedures to a reasonable extent'.

If not met: processing allowed only 'when all of the following conditions are met'
Holder: Prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox ('a public authority or another natural or legal person')

If not met: not stated (uses outside the narrowed exception remain prohibited; fines as for Art. 5, s. 2.9.2)
Position: nearest actors: employers and education institutions, public and private (para 260)
Quote: In light of the AI Act’s objective to ensure a high -level of fundamental rights protection, this  exception should be narrowly interpreted.
Note: Narrows reliance on the exception: 'therapeutic uses should be understood to mean uses of  CE-marked medical devices' (para 257); general wellbeing and stress monitoring is not covered, and a system to detect 'burnout or depression' 'would remain prohibited'; 'safety reasons' cover only 'the protection of  life and health', not property (para 258). Examples (p. 89 [printed 84]): assisting employees or students with autism falls within the exception; assessing wellbeing, motivation or satisfaction is prohibited.

Statutory: statutory: EU employment law and national procedures (instrument not named)

Note: Consultation mechanism linking the employer with workers or their representatives before emotion recognition is introduced for medical or safety reasons. The footnote also says such systems 'will require also consent' under data protection law. Borderline report of another instrument; coded because it conditions introduction of the tool.

Level of obligation: statutory power bounded by EU law; non-binding interpretation
Position: public authority: member state
Quote: What constitutes an imminent threat to life or the physical safety of natural persons is ultimately defined and assessed at the level of the Member State based on its national laws, in accordance with EU law
Note: 'This will have to be laid down/referred to  in the laws Member States must adopt' to use the exception. For terrorist threats, the assessment of the threat 'is ma de at national level', but 'a genuine and present or genuine and foreseeable threat' is 'an autonomous notion of U nion law' to be assessed 'independently of national definitions' (para 345). A specific threat must be 'clearly defined , individualised and concrete' (para 342).

Position: nearest actors: law enforcement authorities [inference]
Quote: Generally speaking, a delay is significant at least when the person is likely to have left the place where the biometric data was taken.
Note: Line between prohibited real-time and permitted post-RBI. 'Without a significant delay' is not defined; 'it will have to be assessed on a case -by-case basis'. Para 312: a law enforcement authority that covertly photographs a person and submits it to a database 'for immediate search' 'may fall under the prohibition'.

Statutory: statutory: AI Act Art. 5(1)(h)(iii); Annex II
If not met: as for the Art. 5 prohibitions: fines under s. 2.9.2 (part 1) and interim injunctions in national courts (para 431)
Position: nearest actors: deploying law enforcement authorities and legislating Member States [inference]
Quote: to use real-time RBI for this purpose, the respective criminal offence must be punishable in the Member State concerned by a custodial sentence or a detention order for a maximum period of at least four years.
Note: Annex II gives an 'exhaustive list of serious crimes' (p. 109 [printed 104]); a suspect is a person for whom there are 'serious grounds' and 'sufficient evidence' already gathered (para 350); no European Arrest Warrant is required (para 353). Example (p. 132 [printed 127]): police live facial recognition for neighbourhood burglaries is 'not allowed to be deployed' even if targeted and limited in perimeter and time, because the offence is not listed in Annex II.

Level of obligation: statutory duty ('shall take into account'); guideline wording 'should'
Holder: the law enforcement authority deploying the system (passive in para 359; para 363 places the assessment in the FRIA 'that the law enforcement authority is obliged to complete')
Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement authority
Quote: the seriousness, probability and scale of the harm for natural persons, society and law enforcement purposes that would be caused if the system were not used, should be assessed against the consequences of the use of the system
Note: Pre-use balancing check. Trigger: 'before using the system'. Compares harm if the system is not used against consequences for rights and freedoms. Metrics, qualitative: seriousness linked to proportionality (para 360); scale = 'the number and categories of persons affected' (para 361); probability = likelihood (para 362). Should include 'evaluating whether less intrusive alternative solutions are available'. 'That assessment will be concluded on a case-by-case basis' (para 363).

Statutory: statutory: AI Act Art. 27(4) (fn 213); DPIA under Art. 27 LED, Art. 35 GDPR, Art. 39 EUDPR
Level of obligation: statutory duties (DPIA, FRIA); the division of labour ('should complement') is non-binding interpretation
Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement authority (deployer); EU institutions under the EUDPR [inference]
Quote: the FRIA should complement the DPIA performed by the deployer as data controller
Note: Relation between two impact assessments. 'The FRIA does not replace the existing Data Protection Impact Assessment' (para 371); the FRIA should avoid 'covering aspects already addressed in the DPIA'. Example: 'a DPIA must be conducted when biometric data are processed through new technologies' such as 'CCTV, AI facial recognition, and body -worn cameras' in publicly accessible spaces. Also coded: FRIA entry (Delivery/Design, para 368).

Statutory: statutory: AI Act Art. 27, applied via Art. 5(2)
Level of obligation: statutory duty; the listed content is provisional, non-binding guidance ('should include')
Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement authority
Quote: A description of the RBI use and the deployer’s processes for the use, together with the intended purpose of use
Note: FRIA content, first items. The description should include the name of the deployer, the law enforcement purpose(s), 'the description of the reference database' and sources of biometric data, the technology (provider documentation entry) and 'the legal basis'. Period and frequency: 'deployers must provide a general indication of the intended period of use and the expected frequency'. Categories of persons: the targeted individual, persons in the reference database, and persons present in the surrounding areas. Further content coded separately (risks, accuracy, human oversight, redress).

Level of obligation: statutory duty; non-binding interpretation of the two-step structure

Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement authority; public authority: member-state judicial or independent administrative authority
Quote: a double necessity and proportionality assessment should occur prior to the deployment of any real -time RBI system  in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes
Location: p. 119 [printed 114], s. 10.2.1, para (380); also para (399), p. 123 [printed 118]
Note: Check before each deployment: first by the user in the FRIA; 'Second, in accordance with Article 5(3) AI Act, a judicial or independent administrative authority must also assess the necessity and proportionality'. Compared against: the objectives in Art. 5(1)(h)(i)-(iii) and limits on time, geography and persons (para 379). Metric: necessity and proportionality; 'National authorities need to verify whether the biometric identification is strictly necessary', based on the FRIA (para 399). The authority's grant is coded Decision-making/Design (para 382).

Level of obligation: statutory exception; its conditions use recital language ('should')
If not met: authorisation must be requested 'without undue delay' and within 24 hours (Art. 5(3)); if rejected, use ceases and data are deleted (para 402)
Holder: the law enforcement authority (specifies safeguards for each urgent use); national law (determines safeguards and conditions)
Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement authority; public authority: member state (legislature)
Quote: subject to appropriate safeguards and conditions , as determined in national law and specified in the context of each individual urgent use case by the law enforc ement authority itself.
Note: Urgency means it is 'effectively and objectively impossible to obtain an authorisation before commencing the use' (para 383, quoting Recital 35). Use 'should be restricted to the absolute minimum necessary'. The 24 hours run from when cameras are 'switched on' and the first comparison is made (para 400). Gives the deploying authority itself authority to set safeguards for the urgent use, pending authorisation.

Statutory: statutory: AI Act Art. 12(3)(a) and Art. 19 (as cited in fn 230)

Note: Recording. Logs 'shall include for the high -risk systems mentioned in point 1(a) of Annex III for each use the start and end data and time'. Trigger: each use; retention at least 6 months. A footnote report of other AI Act provisions; coded because it supports the authorisation check (Accountability entry, para 400).

Holder: not stated (passive); nearest: the deployer (law enforcement authority)

Quote: the reference database(s) used for the unauthorized biometric identification must be removed and deleted if it was built specifically for the contested search.
Note: Deletion after a rejected urgent use: 'all the data, including the results and outputs of that use, must be immediately discarded and deleted' (para 402), including images, metadata, templates, comparison and output data (para 404). Note: Human review of outputs: two competent persons separately verify and confirm each identification before any action. Trigger: each identification.
